feature.summary: When the assistant needs permission for an action, an approval card shows what it will do, a risk label and the parameters, with Allow and Deny choices. When it needs facts from you, a question card lets you pick options or type an answer and send. Each app has its own version.

purpose.what_it_does: Approval cards stop a tool call until the person allows or denies it (once, for this chat, or always where the scope is offered). Question cards (clarify.v1) show up to four questions with up to four options each and an optional 'something else' box; the answers go back to the assistant as the next turn input. (apps/web/features/chat/components/approvals/ToolApprovalCard.tsx:57-140; apps/web/lib/services/clarify-tool-service.ts:12-16; apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/cards/ClarifyCard.tsx:86-229)
purpose.why_it_exists: Consent must be explicit before an action that changes things, and a vague request is better answered with a few structured questions than with a guess. (doc: AGENTS.md section 9; area brief S22.28, S22.29)
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone using an agent that calls tools (all six apps) and anyone whose request is vague (web, desktop, mobile, Chrome, VS Code; CLI shows tool-server questions).
problems_solved: The person sees the tool name, risk tier, destructive notice and parameters before saying yes.
The assistant does not guess missing details; it asks.
A tool server can ask for typed input (CLI elicitation) without leaving the terminal.
use_cases: A cloud tool wants to send data to a connector; the card shows the parameters and the person presses Allow once.
A vague request 'plan my trip' triggers a card with questions about dates and budget; the person picks options and presses Send answers.
In the CLI, a command run asks 'Apply this patch?' with y/n keys.
An MCP server asks for a token; the CLI overlay shows a masked field with Accept, Decline, Cancel.

where_to_find_it: Web and Desktop (hosted web app): approval card is a section labelled 'Approve <tool>' with buttons from the scope labels (Allow once, Allow for this chat, Always allow) and 'Deny' (apps/web/features/chat/components/approvals/ToolApprovalCard.tsx:79-140; packages/contracts/types/src/tool-approval-policy.ts:23-36). Question card is a card in the reply with buttons 'Send answers' and 'I'll just type it' (ClarifyCard.tsx:195-216).

Mobile: approval controls with 'Raw JSON' toggle, guidance field and decision buttons (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/CloudToolApprovalControls.tsx:260-410). Question card with 'Send answers' and 'I'll just type it' (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/ClarifyCard.tsx).

CLI: full-screen approval overlay titled 'Tool Approval' with keys y, n, s, a, d, t and Tab to add a note; MCP request overlay with Accept, Decline, Cancel (apps/cli/src/tui/widgets/approval_overlay.rs:1-30; elicitation_overlay.rs:1-25,375).

VS Code: approval card with approve/deny style buttons and a guidance field; question card titled 'AGI asks' with option buttons, 'Skip' and a typed-answer box (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/sidebar-webview/webviewContent.ts:7262-7360).

Chrome side panel: approval with 'Approve', 'Decline', 'Allow for this chat' and a guidance field (apps/extension/_locales/en/messages.json:1154-1170,1942; apps/extension/src/features/side-panel/bubbles.ts:946-1042); question card built by buildClarifyCard (apps/extension/src/features/side-panel/interactiveCards.ts; bubbles.ts:245).
prerequisites: Question cards need a saved chat (not temporary) and a finished reply; otherwise the controls are disabled (InteractiveCardBlock.tsx:60-86).
An approval card is live only while its turn is live; an expired turn shows no buttons (MessageBubble.tsx:1010-1019).
screens_and_controls: Web approval: label, risk badge (Low/Medium/High/Critical risk), destructive notice, parameter list, 'Raw JSON' details, decision group (ToolApprovalCard.tsx:79-140; packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/tool-approval-presentation.ts:16-23).
Web question card: question text with header chip, option chips (toggle, multi-select where allowed), 'Something else…' box, Send answers, I'll just type it (ClarifyCard.tsx:129-216).

CLI approval: buttons Yes, No, Allow Session, Always allow, Deny All, Allow All; Enter confirms; Esc means No; scroll keys; allow answers are accepted only after the whole detail has been scrolled into view (approval_overlay.rs:1-30,754-822).
journey: The assistant requests a tool call or asks questions.
The card or overlay appears with the details.
The person reads, then chooses an option (or types an answer).
The app sends the decision; the card shows the outcome (for example 'Answered: ...', 'Skipped', or the saved decision) and the assistant continues.
feedback_and_outputs: While streaming the card says 'Available when the reply finishes.'; in a temporary chat it says 'Buttons that send a message work in saved chats.' (InteractiveCardBlock.tsx:60-61).
A failed submit is stored on the message and shown as a red alert on the card (InteractiveCardBlock.tsx:95-102; ClarifyCard.tsx:219-224).
Expired question card: 'These questions are no longer answerable: ...' with a reason (ClarifyCard.tsx:100-112).
Mobile failure text: 'Couldn't send that answer, the questions are still waiting for you.' (apps/mobile ClarifyCard.tsx:28-29).
settings: Tool allowances per chat and always-allow lists (useChatToolAllowanceStore, MessageBubble.tsx:2331-2340).
CLI approval scopes depend on whether session or always-allow is available (approval_overlay.rs:811-816).
Settings, Connectors reset of tool approvals is mentioned in the scope note (tool-approval-presentation.ts:31-32).

established.statement: Actions needing consent render an approval form (what will happen, approve/deny).
The assistant can ask structured questions (options/fields) the user answers in an inline form.
A card cannot be sent while the reply is still streaming; the text says 'Available when the reply finishes.'
A card cannot be sent in a temporary chat; the text says 'Buttons that send a message work in saved chats.'
A failed submission is stored on the message and shown on the card.
The CLI approval overlay is keyboard-driven.
An action a user cannot undo asks first and the question names the consequence.

acceptance_criteria: A tool call that needs approval shows its name, risk label and parameters and cannot run until Allow or Deny is chosen.
Choosing a wider scope on a destructive tool asks for confirmation first on web.
A question card with one selected option and Send answers produces an answered state showing the chosen labels.
'I'll just type it' dismisses the card with the dismissed note.
The card is not answerable while streaming or in a temporary chat and shows the stated message.
A failed submit leaves the card answerable and shows an alert.
In the CLI, y and n answer; Esc answers No; Allow keys are ignored until the detail is fully shown.
An expired card shows the reason text and has no buttons.
inferred: Every app should show the same approval facts (tool, risk, parameters) because the shared labels live in contracts. [inferred from packages/contracts/types/src/tool-approval-policy.ts]
Questions in Local mode would need a local tool; none found. [inferred]
proposed: [proposed] Give VS Code and Chrome the same multi-question form as web.
[proposed] Show clarify questions in the CLI from the model, not only from MCP servers.

steps.what_happens: The model calls the clarify tool or a tool needing approval; the server builds a card and streams it with the reply.
The app validates the card, shows it, and blocks sending while streaming or in a temporary chat.
The person's answer is posted to the respond route, which checks the card and updates the stored message.
The paused turn resumes with the answer.
CLI approval and elicitation are answered on the device and returned to the local agent loop or MCP server.

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: The question card needs the model to call the clarify tool; this is a server tool. The cards themselves do not depend on a provider. Which providers support the tool in the server loop was not traced: unknown.

access_and_usage.account: Web and mobile cards need a signed-in saved chat. CLI approval needs no account (local overlay).
access_and_usage.permissions: Approvals gate tool execution; risk tier and destructive flag come from a review object (tool-approval-presentation.ts:8-14). Unreviewed tools default to high risk, destructive, once-only.
access_and_usage.subscription: none found in the code for the cards; the turn is governed by SYS-subscriptions-entitlements-and-usage.
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: Max 4 questions, 4 options, option label 60, question text 200 characters (clarify-tool-service.ts:15-20); other-answer cap CLARIFY_OTHER_MAX_LENGTH (ClarifyCard.tsx:17). The clarify tool is offered only for short messages without URL, code fence or attachment (clarify-tool-service.ts:49-60). Respond route imports rate limit and CSRF helpers (route.ts:13-14).
access_and_usage.model_compatibility: Any model that can call the clarify tool [inferred]. Not tied to a model.
access_and_usage.local_mode: CLI approval overlay works on the device. Question cards come from a server tool, so a fully Local chat would not show them [inferred]; not verified.

corrections.claim: The clarify tool is 'offered only for short messages without URL, code fence or attachment (clarify-tool-service.ts:49-60)'
corrections.what_the_code_shows: turnWarrantsClarifyTool also returns false for research turns, empty messages, messages over 400 characters, and (unless work_mode is agiwork) messages that open with an explicit verb such as search, write, explain, fix, list. The 4/4/200/60 limits are right.
corrections.correction: The clarify tool is offered only for non-research messages of 1 to 400 characters with no attachment, no URL and no code fence, and (outside AGI Work mode) not starting with an explicit-command verb.

corrections.claim: Questions are a feature for 'web, desktop, mobile, Chrome, VS Code'; the clarify tool is a server tool that gates only on the message
corrections.what_the_code_shows: The server offers the tool only when the surface is web, mobile or chrome, the model can use tools, the request streams, and the client declares x_interactive_cards support for clarify.v1. VS Code and CLI never get it. The VS Code 'AGI asks' card is a separate request/response path (respondToApproval), not clarify.v1.
corrections.correction: The model-driven clarify tool is offered only on web (and desktop via hosted web), mobile and Chrome, and only for streamed, tool-capable turns whose client advertises clarify.v1. The VS Code question card does not come from clarify.v1, so the section 10 gap 'render clarify.v1 fully in VS Code' is misframed.

corrections.claim: Respond route 'soft-delete column used in the lookup (route.ts:31)'
corrections.what_the_code_shows: Line 31 is inside findQuestion. The deleted_at checks are in the SQL on the conversation lookup (about line 117-123) and the message lookup (about line 133).
corrections.correction: Soft-delete is checked on both web_conversations and web_messages in the lookups at route.ts:117-135.

corrections.claim: Respond route errors at route.ts:43,58,93 ('Interactive card not found', 'no longer accepting a response', 'changed while in flight')
corrections.what_the_code_shows: Lines 43, 58 and 93 are inside toClarifyAnswer and settleClarifyBody. The three messages are at about lines 146, 165 and 212.
corrections.correction: Cite route.ts:146, 165 and 212. The route also rejects a card that is not an answer-ui card when payload.kind is message, with 'This card does not send messages'.

corrections.claim: Respond route 'checks the card and updates the stored message' (server step; also 'rate limit and CSRF helpers imported')
corrections.what_the_code_shows: The helpers are used, not only imported: getUserScopedDb auth, requireCsrfToken, and withRateLimit with the 'chat-message' bucket. Update is optimistic: it matches the old metadata with 'is not distinct from' and returns 409 if no row changed. A payload.kind 'message' response does not write anything; it only returns composed text from an answer-ui card.
corrections.correction: The route authenticates the user, requires a CSRF token, applies the chat-message rate limit, then either returns composed message text (answer-ui, nothing stored) or settles the clarify card with a compare-and-set update.

corrections.what_the_code_shows: It is imported at ClarifyCard.tsx:14, not 17. The value (500) is defined in packages/contracts/types/src/interactive-cards.ts:84, which also sets header max 32 and 4 questions/4 options. The page never gives the number.
corrections.correction: Other-answer text is capped at 500 characters (CLARIFY_OTHER_MAX_LENGTH, interactive-cards.ts:84).

missing_facts: The clarify tool is gated server-side: only web, mobile and chrome surfaces, tool-capable models, streaming requests, and clients that declare clarify.v1 in x_interactive_cards (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/request-processor.ts:1278-1291). The page says this is only 'a server tool' and lists VS Code as a user.

The respond route also handles payload.kind 'message' for answer-ui cards: it composes follow-up text and stores nothing (apps/web/app/api/interactive-cards/respond/route.ts:152-160). It uses optimistic concurrency on the metadata update (route.ts:196-217).

Interactive cards are capped at 4 per message and 12,000 serialized characters (packages/contracts/types/src/interactive-cards.ts:13-14), and the other-answer limit is 500 characters (line 84). The page's limits list omits all three.
